subject: Genetics
title: Translocations
description: A micro-lesson that makes Translocations usable.

hook.text: Two chromosomes swap pieces. The carrier may be fine—but their children face high risks of disability.

buildup.text: Balanced translocations keep all genes in the right amounts—just in wrong places. Often no symptoms at all.

discovery.text: Unbalanced forms appear in offspring who get only part of the swap. Missing or extra genes cause disease.

twist.text: The Philadelphia chromosome—a swap between chromosomes 9 and 22—causes chronic myeloid leukemia.

climax.text: Translocations prove gene order and position matter. Same genes in the wrong place cause disease.

punchline.text: Same genes. Wrong place. Different outcome.

quiz.question: What is the Philadelphia chromosome?
options: A translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22 causing leukemia
